title: Complexity Curve Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Set the degree of a polynomial fit to noisy data, compare its training and test error, and judge where the model moves from underfitting through a sweet spot to overfitting.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to judge whether a model is underfitting, well fit, or overfitting by comparing its training and test error, and justify a choice of model complexity.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided judgment with immediate feedback from training and test error
keyQuestions: Why does the training error never increase when the degree goes up?
What do the training and test errors look like for an underfit model? For an overfit model?
If two degrees have nearly the same test error, which should you choose, and why?
commonMisconceptions: The model with the lowest training error is the best model (training error keeps falling even after the model starts fitting noise).
A more complex model is always more accurate (past the sweet spot, the test error rises).
A curve that passes close to every training point has learned the pattern (it may have memorized the noise and will predict new points badly).
The best degree is a fixed property of the data (with a small test set it changes from sample to sample).
assessmentOpportunities: Given a table of training and test MSE for five models of increasing complexity, students label each model as underfitting, a good fit, or overfitting, choose one model, and justify the choice by referring to both errors and to model simplicity.
